item.title: Space Intelligence: The Foundation of Space Superiority
item.description: Space superiority depends on knowing what adversaries can do and recognizing when their behavior changes. Persistent collection and analysis across government, industry, and allies can help anticipate threats before they materialize.

item.title: The Economic Engine of Enduring Space Power
item.description: For enduring space superiority, the United States will need to ensure its space companies are best positioned to capitalize on broader global space markets and dominate spaceborne commerce.

item.title: Trump’s Space Superiority Executive Order: The Stressors That Will Shape Deep Space Development
item.description: What will sustain a lunar economy after astronauts return? Trump’s space executive order sets ambitious deadlines, but a lasting U.S. presence will depend on sustained demand, investment, and clear rules for operating on the Moon.

item.title: What Is Space Superiority?
item.description: What did CENTCOM mean when it declared space superiority over Iran? Joint and Space Force doctrine give different answers, while leaving unresolved who can make that declaration and what evidence is needed to support it.

item.title: How Commercial Industry Can Form the Bedrock of Space Superiority
item.description: Commercial space companies provide infrastructure and information essential to U.S. space superiority. Sustaining that advantage requires investment in technical talent and authority for companies to defend their assets in orbit.

item.title: The Importance and Role of Private Venture Capital in Maintaining U.S. Space Superiority
item.description: U.S. space superiority increasingly relies on private venture capital to finance rapid, milestone-driven capabilities. With domestic R&D shifting to the private sector, venture funding absorbs technical risk and fields unpredictable architectures to outpace adversaries.

item.title: Space Weapons: Disclosure Isn’t Enough for Deterrence
item.description: Can disclosing space weapons deter an adversary? Credible deterrence also requires communicating what those weapons can do and what actions could prompt their use, while protecting sensitive technical details.

item.title: The New Sanctioning Russia Act: Optics for Now, Leverage for Later
item.description: The United States just passed a sanctions bill aimed at Russia's oil revenues, but its real leverage may be the tariff abilities embedded inside it. India, the second-largest buyer of Russian crude, may become the law’s first real test.

item.title: CSIS Launches Initiative on European Energy Security
item.description: The Center for Strategic and International Studies today announced the launch of the Powering Forward Initiative, a new five-year research project exploring Europe’s ascending role in global energy policy and transatlantic relations, with a focus on the intersection of energy, security, and technology.
